outline.section: H2: What Are Stretch Marks and Why Do They Form?
outline.guidance: Explain concisely what stretch marks are (striae distensae): tears in the dermis — the deeper layer of skin beneath the epidermis — caused by rapid skin stretching. Clarify that this is why topical treatments have limits: they act on the surface and upper skin layers, not deep in the dermis where the initial damage occurs. Cover the main causes: pregnancy, rapid weight gain or loss, puberty, bodybuilding. Mention that red or purple stretch marks (striae rubrae) are newer and more responsive to treatment than white or silver ones (striae albae). This sets honest expectations for the rest of the post. Include the keyword 'why my stretch marks are red' naturally.

outline.section: H2: Does Coconut Oil Actually Help With Stretch Marks?
outline.guidance: This is the core section — answer the primary keyword question directly and honestly. Structure the answer in two parts: (1) What coconut oil CAN do: it is a rich emollient with high lauric acid content (approximately 49% of its fatty acid profile) that deeply moisturizes, supports the skin barrier, and may improve skin elasticity — which can make skin more resilient to tearing during rapid stretching. Cite a credible source here, for example: Agero AL, Verallo-Rowell VM (2004), 'A randomized double-blind controlled trial comparing extra virgin coconut oil with mineral oil as a moisturizer for mild to moderate xerosis,' Dermatitis, 15(3):109-116 — or a similar peer-reviewed source confirming coconut oil's emollient efficacy. (2) What coconut oil CANNOT do: it cannot penetrate the dermis deeply enough to repair existing collagen ruptures or permanently remove established stretch marks. Acknowledge the Reddit/skeptic perspective fairly — topical treatments do have real limitations — but contextualize: hydration and elasticity support are still meaningful preventive tools. Use 'is coconut oil good for stretch marks' naturally. Avoid overclaiming.

outline.section: H2: How to Use Coconut Oil for Stretch Marks
outline.guidance: Provide a practical, step-by-step application guide. Steps should include: (1) Choose virgin or extra virgin coconut oil for maximum nutrient retention. (2) Apply to clean, slightly damp skin to lock in moisture — ideally after showering. (3) Warm a small amount between palms before applying. (4) Massage in circular motions for 1-2 minutes to stimulate circulation. (5) Apply at least once daily, ideally twice, for consistent results. (6) Be patient — allow 8-12 weeks of consistent use before evaluating results. Note that a coconut oil-infused body lotion can be a more convenient daily alternative to raw coconut oil, especially for larger body areas. outline.section: H2: Do Stretch Marks Ever Go Away Completely?
outline.guidance: Answer this high-volume question directly and empathetically. Explain that stretch marks are a form of permanent scarring in the dermis and do not fully disappear without clinical intervention (laser therapy, microneedling, prescription retinoids). However, they do naturally fade over time — from red/purple to silvery-white — and become much less noticeable. Emphasize that consistent moisturizing and natural oils support this fading process. Acknowledge that many people find stretch marks much less visible after 1-2 years with good skincare habits. The goal is to manage expectations honestly while keeping the reader motivated to maintain a good routine. Use high-volume semantic keywords naturally here.
